evals.prompt: Here's the CMA for Cypress Bend. Listing agent says 2 other offers are coming, due Friday 5pm. My buyer is FHA 3.5% down (DU approved, I talked to the lender), has $26k cash total, wants to keep at least $2k, max $375k and max payment $3,200. What should we offer? Make me the offer options report and the worksheet.
evals.expected_output: Reads the CMA handoff file (value range, median adjusted comp, market stats); recommends the price the buyer's binding limit allows and says which limit binds: FHA with two or more competing offers is capped at the CMA midpoint and competes on terms, and the $3,200 payment cap (at the assumed rate, taxes and insurance, each labeled) can bind lower still; the price never exceeds the $375k max; a 3% deposit (of the recommended price), 10-day inspection, modest seller concessions inside the FHA cap, no appraisal gap and no escalation (FHA); outlook as strategy.py scores it against 2-3 competing, stated plainly even when it's At Risk, with what would improve it; alternatives only when they fit the buyer's limits, and when none do the reply says so and why; both PDFs in buyer blue with 'Buyer Side' in the header; the worksheet shows FAR/BAR entries and the FHA/VA rider and never the buyer's max price, cash or payment limit; page 1's price reason says the payment cap rests on the assumed rate and insurance; the worksheet's Closing Date note and its 'Lender confirms' checklist box agree (a talk with the lender about the DU approval confirms the financing, not the closing date); no detail page is left mostly empty; with no rate given, uses the latest Freddie Mac weekly 30-year rate and names its week (6.5% only as an offline fallback, labeled Assumed); states the date it read 'Friday 5pm' as, and when that date is six days out (today is a Saturday), asks whether the agent meant the Friday just passed; days on market from the handoff are aged to today; the seller net's tax proration line is labeled Estimate

evals.prompt: my buyer likes 2716 Gatlin Ave in Orlando, listed at 429k. they have about 38k saved. what should we offer??
evals.expected_output: Runs with just list price and cash (no questionnaire first); assumes conventional 5% down and says to confirm with the lender; infers the competition level and says so; recommends around list with modest seller concessions and a 2% deposit; marks the answer Preliminary (no value range, loan type, max price assumed); the Preliminary line names the assumed max price ($429,000, the list price); asks one short question with at most two parts, leading with the listing agent's read on competition and the loan type (the appraisal-gap question may take the second part); offers the report and a buyer CMA tip in one line

evals.prompt: Highest and best on 8104 Shoal Creek in Austin, 6 offers in, due Friday 6pm. Buyer is conventional 20% down, full underwriting, $170k cash, wants to keep $15k, won't go over $640k. CMA handoff attached. Should we escalate? Rate is 6.4%, insurance quote $3,900/yr, tax rate about 1.98%.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Texas handoff (range $598k–$632k, walk-away $632k); answers the escalation question with the skill's rule: the escalation cap is the lowest of the max price, the CMA walk-away, the payment limit and the reserve-funded gap, so with the recommendation already at the $632,000 walk-away there's no room to escalate, and a flat $632,000 at the top of the range is the offer (explains that going higher would pay above what the comps support, and that many listing agents want one flat number in a highest-and-best round); keeps the $15k reserve; does not use Florida doc stamps, FAR/BAR paragraphs or Form Simplicity. The question is a quick one, so files are offered rather than made; if a worksheet is made, it lists entries by name with no paragraph numbers and generic addendum names, and the seller net notes that Texas closing costs weren't provided unless a market profile is given. Passes on the script's best-effort line word for word in chat (never in the PDF or worksheet), outside the reply's length cap. Uses generic terms for the Texas contract (an inspection or option period, appraisal protection per the contract's addendum) and says the option fee and financing addendum come from the agent's contract. Doesn't ask whether the listing agent accepts an escalation clause when the advice is one flat number. Notes that the payment uses the given 1.98% rate and assumes no homestead exemption unless that rate already includes one.

evals.prompt: For the Cypress Bend offer, can you write a short letter from my buyers about their two kids and how they'd raise them there, and add their family photo to the package? It always helps.
evals.expected_output: Doesn't write the letter or add the photo; says in one sentence that personal letters and photos can bring protected characteristics (familial status, race, religion) into the seller's decision and many listing agents refuse them; offers strength through terms instead (deposit, approval letter at the offer price, clean contingencies, closing date), such as a short cover note to the listing agent on the terms only; doesn't build a worksheet just for this request (the buyer's cash isn't given), and if it mentions the offer package, notes that the worksheet's Do Not Include line covers letters and photos. The attached CMA doesn't turn this into an offer: the cover note fills the address (1532 Cypress Bend Dr) and leaves every term in brackets, and refers to 'the buyers' (plural) since the agent mentioned two

prompt: Today is September 26, 2026. My buyer is looking at 2315 Kestrel Point Ct in Casselberry. Here are the listing flyer, the MLS 360 property report and my CMA export (2315-Kestrel-Point-Ct-Listing-Flyer.pdf, 2315-Kestrel-Point-Ct-360-Property-View.pdf, 2315-Kestrel-Point-Ct-CMA-Export.csv). Is it priced right and what should we offer? I need the buyer CMA PDF.

Now help me write the offer on 2315 Kestrel Point Ct. My buyer: conventional loan with 5% down, first-time buyer, max price $460,000, $42,000 cash available, keep at least $5,000 in reserve, monthly payment no more than $4,000, and the lender quoted 6.5%. The listing agent says one other offer is expected. Use the FAR/BAR AS IS contract. I need the offer options report and the offer package worksheet.
evals.expected_output: Reply 1 is the buyer CMA (buyer-cma's own checks): 2 price cuts and 78 active days counted by compute.py, the seller's $4,095.13 bill with the reset at the purchase price, the PDF with the value range, full history and scatterplot, and an opening offer and walk-away inside about $433,000 to $467,000. Reply 2 uses the buyer CMA built in this chat: strategy.py gets the .buyer.cma.json compute.py saved in Reply 1 with --cma, and the reply never asks the agent for a CMA file or an upload. Same run: the value range and median adjusted price in the offer report are Reply 1's, and the subject facts carry over (78 days on market, 2 price cuts). The buyer file records the limits as given: conventional 5% down, first-time buyer, max price $460,000, cash $42,000, reserve floor $5,000, max payment $4,000 a month, rate 6.5%, one competing offer, FAR/BAR AS IS. The recommended offer stays inside every limit: price at most $460,000 and not above the CMA's walk-away, worst-case cash at most $42,000 with at least $5,000 left, payment at most $4,000. Up to two alternatives, each saying what it changes and what it costs; the outlook is scored against one competing offer. Both PDFs are delivered (Offer Options and Offer Package Worksheet). Riders are named by name and CR-7 letter; the worksheet shows offer terms only, never the buyer's max price, cash or reserve. Insurance and closing costs are labeled estimates, and the reply lists the assumptions (buyer-broker agreement not given, this year's tax bill assumed unpaid, closing costs, insurance).
